primary_cause: Rate-crash pressure on Schwab earnings model. Earnings depend heavily on net interest revenue and sweep cash economics. 10-year hit ~0.318% 2-year ~0.285%
secondary_factors: Broad financials selloff recession panic and liquidity and fund-flow fears. Markets even discussing possibility of negative U.S. rates
store_description: Schwab fell more than the market because the March 9 bond move was extreme even by crisis standards. The 10-year Treasury hit roughly 0.318% and the 2-year fell to about 0.285% directly threatening spread-based revenue for brokers and banks. With markets pricing emergency Fed easing and even flirting with negative-rate talk SCHW's drop looks primarily like a rate-sensitivity repricing.

primary_cause: COVID demand disruption to store traffic especially international and urban exposure. Already disclosed 2000+ China stores closed and hurt China traffic
secondary_factors: Worsening global mobility restrictions as virus spread beyond China with Italy locking down millions. General consumer discretionary de-risking
store_description: Starbucks was already a known coronavirus casualty before Crash Monday because China is a major growth market and the company had warned of a hit from widespread store closures. As the crisis shifted from China to Europe and the U.S. investors repriced Starbucks as a global foot-traffic business facing a sharper revenue shock.

primary_cause: Commercial aerospace exposure through pending Raytheon-UTC combination via Pratt & Whitney and Collins. Travel demand cratering
secondary_factors: Broader industrials selloff and virus-driven airline stress
store_description: Unlike pure-play defense names RTX had meaningful commercial aerospace sensitivity through the United Technologies merger so the virus shock to airline traffic mattered. With travel demand collapsing and recession fears exploding on March 9 the drop looks mainly like a commercial aerospace de-rating rather than a defense-specific issue.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Mar 2 Qualcomm said coronavirus threatened phone industry and forecast handset demand and supply disruptions would hurt the quarter
secondary_factors: March 9 semiconductor-wide selloff with SOX down 8.3% amplified the move
store_description: Qualcomm had a genuine company-specific catalyst because management explicitly warned that coronavirus disruption threatened the phone market even though its revenue outlook was otherwise relatively solid. By March 9 that warning was amplified by an 8.3% drop in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.

primary_cause: Previously disclosed coronavirus operational hit — Feb 20 P&G warned COVID would hurt current-quarter revenue and profit via supply-chain disruption and weaker China demand
secondary_factors: Broad defensive-selling despite staple status on Crash Monday. No new Mar 6-9 company update
store_description: P&G's drop was smaller than many cyclicals which fits its defensive profile but investors still had a live fundamental issue: management had already warned China-related disruption would dent results. On Crash Monday that known earnings headwind was compounded by market-wide liquidation.

primary_cause: No clear Pfizer-specific negative catalyst. Broad market and healthcare ETF and liquidity selling
secondary_factors: Recession fear and cross-asset deleveraging. Relatively modest decline consistent with defensive pharma profile
store_description: Pfizer's decline was relatively modest versus the market which is what you would expect for a large pharmaceutical name with no obvious fresh negative company event in the March 6-9 window. The move looks more like indiscriminate risk-off selling than a Pfizer-specific repricing.

primary_cause: Semiconductor sector selloff tied to COVID and recession fears. SOX fell 8.3% on March 9
secondary_factors: China exposure and hardware-cycle sensitivity. No discrete Nvidia announcement in the 3-day window
store_description: Nvidia was sold as part of a broad semiconductor unwind rather than on fresh company news. With markets suddenly pricing a deeper global downturn and severe supply-chain disruption investors hit cyclical growth semis hard.

primary_cause: Fear of elective-procedure deferrals as hospitals moved toward postponing procedures and preparing for COVID
secondary_factors: General growth and medtech selloff on Crash Monday. Business depends on procedure volume
store_description: Intuitive's business depends on procedure volume so the market quickly recognized that a pandemic could suppress surgeries even before formal nationwide shutdowns were fully in place. That made ISRG more vulnerable than big pharma on March 9.

primary_cause: Sector-wide semiconductor selloff on recession fears. Especially exposed to analog demand from industrial and automotive end markets
secondary_factors: SOX down 8.3% on March 9. No TXN-specific corporate event in prior 3 days
store_description: TI is especially exposed to analog demand from industrial and auto customers exactly the end markets investors expected to weaken in a sudden global downturn. With the SOX down 8.3% on March 9 TXN's drop looks primarily macro and sector-driven.

primary_cause: Semiconductor-sector de-rating on COVID supply and demand fears. Semis one of most aggressively de-risked groups on Crash Monday
secondary_factors: Broad tech liquidation and cyclical exposure. No fresh Intel-specific announcement
store_description: Intel sold off harder than the S&P because semis were one of the market's most aggressively de-risked groups on Crash Monday. With investors assuming both supply-chain disruption and weaker global electronics demand INTC's decline fits the sector move more than any company-specific event.

primary_cause: Global cyclical and recession exposure intensified by collapsing energy capex expectations. Oil crashed roughly 24-25%. Sits at intersection of construction mining industrial activity and energy spending
secondary_factors: China and industrial slowdown fears and indiscriminate industrial selling on Crash Monday
store_description: March 9 was especially bad for Caterpillar because the stock sits at the intersection of construction mining industrial activity and energy spending. When oil crashed roughly 24-25% and recession fears exploded CAT was repriced as a high-beta global industrial which explains the very steep 14.3% decline.

primary_cause: Bank net-interest-margin pressure plus credit and recession fears. 10-year yield touching roughly 0.318% crushed earnings outlook for rate-sensitive banks
secondary_factors: Cross-financial deleveraging and market liquidity stress. No Citi-specific negative announcement
store_description: Citi's move was one of the clearest expressions of the March 9 rates and recession shock. The 10-year yield touching roughly 0.318% crushed the earnings outlook for rate-sensitive banks while also raising fears of large future credit losses making the 16.2% drop a bank-specific macro reaction.

primary_cause: Look-through exposure to economically sensitive holdings especially financials industrials and travel-related businesses during violent macro selloff
secondary_factors: Mark-to-market concerns and broad conglomerate discount widening. Cash and defensive qualities limited downside vs banks
store_description: Berkshire was not the biggest loser because of its cash and defensive qualities but the market still marked down its underlying exposure to banks transport industrial activity and consumer demand. On a day when yields collapsed and travel fears intensified BRK-B's decline looks like a portfolio-through-the-looking-glass selloff.

primary_cause: No clear Bristol-specific negative catalyst. Broad market liquidation with less downside than cyclical sectors because pharma was relatively defensive
secondary_factors: Healthcare ETF flows and generalized risk-off on Crash Monday
store_description: BMY's move was material but still smaller than banks airlines or semis which fits the absence of a company-specific shock. The stock appears to have been pulled lower by the broader March 9 liquidation rather than by trial regulatory or guidance news.

primary_cause: Asset-manager sensitivity to market declines since sharp drop in global asset values threatens fee revenue
secondary_factors: Financials weakness and client de-risking and cash rotation on Crash Monday
store_description: BlackRock was sold as both a financial and an asset-based-fee business on a day when markets were collapsing across equities and credit. Even without a company-specific announcement the combination of lower AUM higher volatility and risk-off positioning supports the 7.0% drop.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Mar 9 Booking withdrew Q1 guidance because of worsening COVID travel demand. By Mar 6 travel industry already experiencing collapsing bookings
secondary_factors: Italy lockdown and broader travel-sector panic
store_description: BKNG had one of the strongest stock-specific catalysts because management explicitly pulled Q1 guidance as travel demand worsened especially in North America and Europe. That came on the same day investors were digesting Italy's lockdown and a global travel freeze making the move directly tied to fundamentals.

primary_cause: Financial-sector selloff driven by collapsing rates and recession fear. Fee and AUC sensitivity to falling markets and systemic liquidity stress
secondary_factors: No BNY Mellon-specific announcement in the 3-day window
store_description: BNY Mellon was pressured by the same forces hitting the whole financial complex: record-low yields recession fear and falling market values that can hurt custody and servicing economics. The 8.2% drop looks mostly like a rates-plus-risk-off reaction not a BK-specific headline.

primary_cause: Severe yield-curve collapse hitting bank earnings power. 10-year briefly at 0.318%. Investors discussing negative-rate scenarios. NIM expectations marked down aggressively
secondary_factors: Broad financial deleveraging and recession and credit fears
store_description: BAC traded as a pure macro and rates casualty on March 9. With the 10-year briefly at 0.318% and investors suddenly discussing negative-rate scenarios the market aggressively marked down NIM expectations while also pricing a future rise in credit losses.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Reuters reported FAA rejected Boeing's proposal to leave certain 737 MAX wiring bundles in place potentially delaying return to service
secondary_factors: Pandemic shock to airlines and aerospace layered on top of pre-existing MAX crisis
store_description: BA was one of the few names with a same-day company-specific negative headline: Reuters said the FAA would not back Boeing's proposed fix on MAX wiring and the stock fell about 12% on that news. Layer in the coronavirus collapse in airline demand and Boeing's 13.4% decline is much more company-specific than just the market.

primary_cause: Anticipated hit to billed business from travel-and-entertainment spending collapse. Unusually exposed to rapid collapse in T&E spending
secondary_factors: Consumer-credit and recession fears and financials selloff. No Mar 6-9 company release
store_description: Even before AmEx quantified it later in March the market could already see that one of its most valuable spending categories business and travel was deteriorating rapidly. That made AXP more vulnerable than many other payment names on Crash Monday.
